title: ARTEX Explained
subtitle: Eight cards on an AI team that pentests on its own, before the full lesson.

cards.headline: Not a smarter scanner. A team that remembers.
cards.body: ARTEX runs a penetration test with a team of AI agents that plan, work, record what they learn and know when to stop. The difference from a chatbot with tools is the memory and the roles.

cards.headline: Four roles you will meet
points: Goals agent: turns the brief into goals
Planner: writes work orders and keeps the to-do list
Workers: run real tools and record facts
Main agent: holds the loop together

cards.headline: Shared graphs are the team's memory
cards.body: An exploration graph of what was found and tried, an asset graph of what exists, facts with evidence, findings built from facts. Nobody repeats work; nobody forgets a lead.

cards.headline: Autonomy inside a fence
cards.body: Authorized scope, approval gates for risky actions, a traffic recorder, a human operator who can say no. The planner's decisions live inside those rails.

cards.headline: Ten wake-ups, ten decisions
cards.body: Step into the team lead's seat: what should the team do next, given its state? Every option explained, right or wrong.

cards.headline: When the loop stops, the records tell you where
cards.body: A lab task made no progress overnight. Use the team's own notes, graphs and work orders to find which part of the loop was waiting, and on what.

cards.headline: What this lesson covers
cards.body: Tap any line to jump back to its card.

cards.headline: Start with the map
cards.body: Chapter 1 lays out the agent team, its memory and its guard rails on one map you rebuild from memory.
